title: DOES TERRORISM TRIGGER ONLINE HATE SPEECH? ON THE ASSOCIATION OF EVENTS AND TIME SERIES
benchmark_measurement: The paper measures the systematic statistical association between offline Islamist terrorist attacks and online bursts of hate speech and counter-hate speech, specifically anti-Muslim hate speech (#stopislam), Muslim counter-hate speech (#notinmyname), and jihadist hate speech (kafir).
findings: The analysis shows that Islamist terrorist attacks in Western Europe and North America systematically trigger bursts of anti-Muslim hate speech on Twitter (#stopislam). However, the study does not provide evidence for a systematic association between these attacks and peaks in jihadist hate speech (kafir) or Muslim counter-hate speech (#notinmyname) over the study period (2015-2017).
